title: Rolling Bearing Fault Severity Recognition via Data Mining Integrated With Convolutional Neural Network
dataset: lab experimental bearing signals; signals collected from a wind turbine simulator with faulty high-speed shaft roller bearing
method: impulse mining and fault recognition; matrix profile (MP); convolutional neural network (CNN) combined with softmax regression
reported_metrics: The results demonstrate that the proposed method can better recognize the fault severities of rolling bearings than the comparison methods.

title: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection Method for Bearing Based on VAE-GAN and Time-Series Data Correlation Enhancement (June 2023)
dataset: laboratory datasets and actual wind turbine datasets
method: temporal convolutional variational autoencoder—generative adversarial networks (TCVAE-GAN)
reported_metrics: The validation results obtained from both the laboratory datasets and actual wind turbine datasets demonstrate the high sensitivity of our method in detecting early weak faults in bearings.

title: Multi-Scale and multi-level feature enhanced meta-learning for few-shot fault diagnosis
dataset: Paderborn bearing dataset and the LUT-WFD wind turbine fault dataset
signal_type: time-frequency representations and raw temporal vibration signals
method: a dual-branch meta-learning fault diagnosis framework with multi-scale and multi-level feature enhancement
reported_metrics: Extensive experiments conducted on the Paderborn bearing dataset and the LUT-WFD wind turbine fault dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior diagnostic accuracy under few-shot learning, strong noise interference, and cross-condition transfer scenarios.

title: Machine Learning Techniques for Wind Turbine Predictive Maintenance Using SCADA Data
dataset: real SCADA data of three 2.1 MW wind turbines located in northeastern Brazil
method: Multiple Linear Regression (MLR); eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost); Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks; statistical process control
reported_metrics: XGBoost provides the most consistent overall performance, achieving R2 values up to 0.92 and MAPE below 2.2% for generator bearing prediction, while LSTM achieved R2 up to 0.99 and MAPE below 0.5% in specific gearbox cases
